correctness.rationale: A completed one-run bracketed by zeros has length km. Its visible preceding zero-run cannot exceed m, and if that zero-run is left-bracketed by a one it must have length exactly m (too short would expose the second forbidden family, too long the third). For a terminal one-run following a left-bracketed zero-run of length a, its visible length is at most ka. Conversely, these constraints let one fill the first and last partial runs into generators: an initial one-run can be a suffix of any sufficiently long generator, an initial zero-run can be lengthened as required, and a terminal zero-run can always be completed. This also treats words consisting of a single run. Thus avoidance suffices. Both one-letter end deletions of every proposed obstruction occur, including 0^m1^(km)0 across a generator boundary and 0^(m+1)1^(km) in a larger generator; this proves minimality. The lengths are r+2 and (k+1)m+2, giving the series, including cancellation for k=1. Intersecting with 10^+1^+ and pumping in the initial 1/zero-run proves nonregularity for every k. Bounded but infinitely often positive counts give growth entropy zero. In a separate bounded reproduction, I closed the set of concatenation suffixes of length at most 15 under appending generators with m<=16, collected factors through length 16 from each suffix-plus-generator, and identified absent words with admissible prefix and suffix of length one less. Larger generators can be replaced by m=16 for this bounded factor census (all observed runs or run fragments in such a generator still fit). The family lists matched for k=1,...,6, with respective cumulative counts 14, 15, 16, 15, 16, 16. This check does not prove the unbounded statement. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration is bounded; the proof uses run extension for the unrestricted language.
